nodes.name: Eskin-Mirzakhani closed Teichmuller geodesic count
nodes.statement: A recent famous result of Eskin and Mirzakhani \cite{EM}, which served as a motivation for this note, shows that for the moduli space $\mathcal M_g$ of a closed oriented surface $S_g$ of genus $g\ge 2$, the number $N(R)$ of closed Teichmuller geodesics in $\mathcal M_g$ of length $\le R$ grows as $N(R)\sim \frac{e^{hR}}{hR}$ as $R\to\infty$ where $h=6g-6$.
nodes.statement_short: Number of closed Teichmuller geodesics of length at most R in moduli space grows like e^{hR}/(hR), h=6g-6.
assumptions: for the moduli space $\mathcal M_g$ of a closed oriented surface $S_g$ of genus $g\ge 2$
conclusions: the number $N(R)$ of closed Teichmuller geodesics in $\mathcal M_g$ of length $\le R$ grows as $N(R)\sim \frac{e^{hR}}{hR}$ as $R\to\infty$ where $h=6g-6$

nodes.name: stretch factor of a fully irreducible
nodes.statement: Every fully irreducible element $\varphi\in Out(F_N)$ has a well-defined \emph{stretch factor} $\lambda(\varphi)>1$ (see \cite{BH}) which is an invariant of the $Out(F_N)$-conjugacy class of $\varphi$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1.1 (exponential count of conjugacy classes of fully irreducibles in Out(F_N))
nodes.statement:
Let $N\ge 3$.  Let $S$ be a finite generating set for $Out(F_N)$.
There exist constants $\sigma>1$ and $C_2>C_1>0$, $R_0\ge 1$ such that the following hols.
For $R\ge 0$ let $B_R$ be the ball of radius $R$ in the Cayley graph of $Out(F_N)$ with respect to $S$.

Denote by $c_R$ the number of distinct $Out(F_N)$-conjugacy classes of fully irreducible elements $\varphi\in B_R$ such that $C_1R\le \log\lambda(\varphi)\le C_2 R$.
Then
\[
c_R\ge \sigma^R
\]
for all $R\ge R_0$.
nodes.statement_short: For N>=3, the number of Out(F_N)-conjugacy classes of fully irreducibles in the R-ball with log stretch factor ~R grows exponentially.
assumptions: Let $N\ge 3$.
Let $S$ be a finite generating set for $Out(F_N)$.
conclusions: There exist constants $\sigma>1$ and $C_2>C_1>0$, $R_0\ge 1$ such that the following hols.
c_R\ge \sigma^R
for all $R\ge R_0$.
nodes.label: thm:A

nodes.name: Theorem 1.2 (exponential conjugacy growth of loxodromics for WPD actions)
nodes.statement:
Suppose $G$ has a cobounded WPD action on a hyperbolic metric space $X$ and $L$ is a non-elementary subgroup of $G$ for this action. Let $S$ be a generating set of $G$. 
For $R\ge 1$ let $b_R$ be the number of distinct $G$-conjugacy classes of elements of $g\in L$ that act loxodromically on $X$ and such that $|g|_S\le R$. Then there exist $R_0\ge 1$ and $c>1$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$
\[
b_R\ge c^R.
\]
nodes.statement_short: For a cobounded WPD action, the number of conjugacy classes of loxodromics of word length at most R in a non-elementary subgroup grows exponentially.
assumptions: $G$ has a cobounded WPD action on a hyperbolic metric space $X$
$L$ is a non-elementary subgroup of $G$ for this action
Let $S$ be a generating set of $G$.
conclusions: there exist $R_0\ge 1$ and $c>1$ such that for all $R\ge R_0$
b_R\ge c^R.
nodes.label: thm:B

nodes.name: Hull-Osin exponential conjugacy growth
nodes.statement: Theorem~\ref{thm:B} is a generalization of \cite[Theorem 1.1]{HO}, which states (under a different but equivalent hypothesis, see \cite{O}) that such $G$ has exponential conjugacy growth.
conclusions: such $G$ has exponential conjugacy growth

nodes.name: Theorem 1.3 (hyperbolically embedded free subgroups in non-elementary subgroups)
nodes.statement:
Suppose $G$ has a cobounded WPD action on a hyperbolic metric space $X$ and $L$ is a non-elementary subgroup of $G$ for this action. Then for every $n\ge 2$ there exists a subgroup $H\le L$ and a finite group $K\leq G$ such that: 
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H\cong F_n$.
\item $H\times K\hookrightarrow _h G$.
\item The orbit map $H\to X$ is a quasi-isometric embedding.
\end{enumerate}

In particular, every element of $H$ is loxodromic with respect to the action on $X$ and two elements of $H$ are conjugate in $G$ if and only if they are conjugate in $H$.
nodes.statement_short: A non-elementary subgroup of a cobounded WPD action contains a free subgroup H with H x K hyperbolically embedded and quasi-isometrically embedded orbit map.
assumptions: $G$ has a cobounded WPD action on a hyperbolic metric space $X$
$L$ is a non-elementary subgroup of $G$ for this action
conclusions: for every $n\ge 2$ there exists a subgroup $H\le L$ and a finite group $K\leq G$ such that:
$H\cong F_n$.
$H\times K\hookrightarrow _h G$.
The orbit map $H\to X$ is a quasi-isometric embedding.
every element of $H$ is loxodromic with respect to the action on $X$
two elements of $H$ are conjugate in $G$ if and only if they are conjugate in $H$
nodes.label: thm:C

nodes.name: hyperbolically embedded subgroup notation
nodes.statement: Here for a subgroup $A$ of a group $G$ writing $A\hookrightarrow _h G$ means that $A$ is \emph{hyperbolically embedded in} $G$.

nodes.name: acylindricity of the Out(F_N) action on the free factor complex
nodes.statement: Note that it is still not known whether the action of $Out(F_N)$ on the free factor complex is acylindrical, and, in a sense, the use of Theorem~\ref{thm:B} provides a partial workaround here.

nodes.name: convex cocompact subgroups of Out(F_N) are stable
nodes.statement: It is proved in \cite{ADT} that convex cocompact (that is, finitely generated and with the orbit map to the free factor complex being a quasi-isometric embedding) subgroups of $Out(F_N)$ are \emph{stable} in $Out(F_N)$.
assumptions: convex cocompact (that is, finitely generated and with the orbit map to the free factor complex being a quasi-isometric embedding) subgroups of $Out(F_N)$
conclusions: are \emph{stable} in $Out(F_N)$

nodes.name: stable subgroups have finite width
nodes.statement: In turn, it is proved in \cite{AMST} that if $H$ is a stable subgroup of a group $G$, then $H$ has finite width in $G$ (see \cite{AMST} for the relevant definitions).
assumptions: $H$ is a stable subgroup of a group $G$
conclusions: $H$ has finite width in $G$

nodes.name: H and H x K are stable
nodes.statement: Note that in the conclusion of Theorem~\ref{thm:C} the fact that $H\times K\hookrightarrow _h G$ implies that $H$ and   $H\times K$ are stable in $G$.
assumptions: $H\times K\hookrightarrow _h G$
conclusions: $H$ and   $H\times K$ are stable in $G$

nodes.name: infinite critical exponent of Out(F_N) on Outer space
nodes.statement: For essentially the same reasons as explained in Remark~\ref{rem:exp} below, the action of $Out(F_N)$ (where $N\ge 3$) on $CV_N$, with either the asymmetric or symmetrized Lipschitz metric, has infinite critical exponent.
assumptions: $N\ge 3$
conclusions: the action of $Out(F_N)$ (where $N\ge 3$) on $CV_N$, with either the asymmetric or symmetrized Lipschitz metric, has infinite critical exponent

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.3
nodes.statement:
First we note that (3) implies that every element of $H$ is loxodromic with respect to the action on $X$. Also, the fact that two elements of $H$ are conjugate in $G$ if and only if they are conjugate in $H$ follows from the fact that $H\times K$ is almost malnormal in $G$ and $K$ acts trivially on $H$ by conjugation.


We  use the construction from [Theorem 6.14]\cite{DGO}. As in  [Theorem 6.14]\cite{DGO}, we let $n=2$ since the construction from this case can be easily modified for any $n$.

By Lemma \ref{lem:MS}, we can assume $X=Cay(G, \mathcal A)$ for some $\mathcal A\subseteq G$. Let $g_1,..., g_6$ be elements of $L$ given by Lemma \ref{L2}. Then each $E(g_i)=\langle g_i\rangle\times K_G(L)$ and furthermore $\{E(g_1),...,E(g_6)\}\hookrightarrow _h (G, \mathcal A)$ by Lemma \ref{L1}. Let $$\mathcal E=\bigcup_{i=1}^6 E(g_i)\setminus\{1\}.$$ Let $H=\langle x, y\rangle$ where  $x=g_1^ng_2^ng_3^n$ and $y=g_4^ng_5^ng_6^n$ for sufficiently large $n$. It is shown in \cite{DGO} that $x$ and $y$ generate a free subgroup of $G$ and this subgroup is quasi-convex in $Cay(G, \mathcal A\cup\mathcal E)$. Hence $H$ (with the natural word metric) is quasi-isometrically embedded in $Cay(G, \mathcal A\cup\mathcal E)$, and since the map $Cay(G, \mathcal A)\to Cay(G, \mathcal A\cup\mathcal E)$ is 1-lipschitz $H$ is also quasi-isometrically embedded in $Cay(G, \mathcal A)$. Let $K=K_G(L)$. Since $x$ and $y$ both commute with $K$, $\langle H, K\rangle \cong H\times K$. Finally, we can apply \cite[Theorem 4.42]{DGO} to get that $H\times K\hookrightarrow _h G$. Verifing the assumptions of \cite[Theorem 4.42]{DGO} is identical to the proof of \cite[Theorem 6.14]{DGO}.

nodes.name: Outer space, free factor complex and Lipschitz metrics
nodes.statement: In what follows we assume that $N\ge 2$ is an integer, $CV_N$ is the (volume-one normalized) Culler-Vogtmann Outer space, $\mathcal F_N$ is the free factor complex for $F_N$, $d_C$ is the asymmetric Lipschitz metric on $CV_N$ and $d^{sym}_C$ is the symmetrized Lipschitz metric on $CV_N$.

nodes.name: Hausdorff distance in Outer space
nodes.statement: When we talk about the Hausdorff distance $d_{Haus}$ in $CV_N$, we always mean the Hausdorff distance with respect to $d^{sym}_C$.

nodes.name: K-quasigeodesic in CV_N
nodes.statement:
For $K\ge 1$, by a $K$-quasigeodesic in $CV_N$ we mean a function $\gamma:I\to CV_N$ (where $I\subseteq \mathbb R$) is an interval, such that for all $s,t\in I, s\le t$ we have
\[
 \frac{1}{K}(t-s)-K \le d_C(\gamma(s),\gamma(t))\le K(t-s)+K.
\]

nodes.name: thick part of Outer space
nodes.statement: For $\epsilon>0$ we denote by $CV_{N,\epsilon}$ the $\epsilon$-thick part of $CV_N$.

nodes.name: Dowdall-Taylor quasigeodesic fellow-travelling (Theorem 4.1 of DT)
nodes.statement_short: Quasigeodesics in Outer space projecting to quasigeodesics in the free factor complex stay thick and fellow-travel geodesics with the same endpoints.
assumptions: Let $K\ge 1$ and let $\gamma:\mathbb R\to CV_N$ be a $K$-quasigeodesic such that its projection $\pi\circ \gamma: \mathbb R\to \mathcal F_N$ is also a $K$-quasigeodesic.
$\rho:\mathbb R\to CV_N$ is any geodesic with the same endpoints as $\gamma$
conclusions: There exist constants $D>0,\epsilon>0$, depending only on $K$ and $N$, such that the following holds:
We have $\gamma(\mathbb R), \rho(\mathbb R)\subset CV_{N,\epsilon}$.
We have $d_{Haus}(\gamma(\mathbb R), \rho(\mathbb R))\le D$.
nodes.label: prop:DT

nodes.name: same endpoints
nodes.statement: Here saying that $\gamma$ and $\rho$ have the same endpoints means that $\sup_{t\in \mathbb R} d_C^{sym}(\gamma(t),\rho(t))<\infty$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
By \cite{BF}, the action of $Out(F_N)$ on $\mathcal F_N$ satisfies the hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:C}. Let $H$ be the subgroup provided by Theorem \ref{thm:C} with $L=Out(F_n)$.

We fix a free basis $\mathcal A=\{a,b\}$ for the free group $H$, and let $d_\mathcal A$ be the corresponding word metric on $H$. 

Note that the assumptions on $H$ imply that every nontrivial element of $H$ is fully irreducible.  Moreover, if we pick a base-point $p$ in $\mathcal F_N$, then there is $K\ge 1$ such that the image of every geodesic in the Cayley graph $Cay(H,\mathcal A)$ in $\mathcal F_N$ under the orbit map is a (parameterized) $K$-quasigeodesic.



 Pick a basepoint $G_0\in CV_N$.
Since the projection $\pi:(CV_N,d_C)\to \mathcal F_N$ is coarsely Lipschitz~\cite{BF}, and since the orbit map $H\to \mathcal F_N$ is a quasi-isometric embedding, it follows that the orbit map $(H,d_\mathcal A)\to (CV_N,d_C), u\mapsto u G_0$ is a $K_1$-quasi-isometric embedding for some $K_1\ge 1$. Moreover, the image of this orbit map lives in an $\epsilon_0$-thick part of $CV_N$ (where $\epsilon_0$ is the injectivity radius of $G_0$). Since on $CV_{N,\epsilon_0}$ the metrics $d_C$ and $d_C^{sym}$ are bi-Lipschitz equivalent, it follows that the orbit map $(H,d_\mathcal A)\to (CV_N,d_C^{sym}), u\mapsto u G_0$ is a $K_2$-quasi-isometric embedding for some $K_2\ge 1$.
For every $c\in \mathcal{A}^{\pm 1}$ fix a $d_C$-geodesic $\tau_c$ from $G_0$ to $cG_0$. 

Now let $\gamma: I\to Cay(H,\mathcal A)$ be a geodesic such that $\gamma^{-1}(H)=I\cap \mathbb Z$ and such that the endpoints of $I$ (if any) are integers. We then define a path $\underline{\gamma}:I\to CV_N$ as follows. Whenever $n\in \mathbb Z$ is such that $[n,n+1]\subseteq I$, then $\gamma(n)=g$ and $\gamma(n+1)=gc$ for some $c\in \mathcal A^{\pm 1}$. In this case we define $\gamma|_{[n,n+1]}$ to be $g\tau_c$.  Then for every geodesic $\gamma: I\to Cay(H,\mathcal A)$ as above the path $\underline{\gamma}:I\to CV_N$ is $K_3$-quasigeodesic, with respect to both $d_C$ and $d_C^{sym}$, for some $K_3\ge 1$ independent of $\gamma$. Moreover, $\underline{\gamma}(I)\subset CV_{N,\epsilon_1}$ for some $\epsilon_1>0$ independent of $\gamma$.


 Let $w$ be a cyclically reduced word of length $n\ge 1$ in $H$. Consider the bi-infinite $w^{-1}$-periodic geodesic $\gamma:\mathbb R\to Cay(H,\mathcal A)$ with $\gamma(0)=1$ and $\gamma(n)=w^{-1}$.   Thus the path the path $\underline{\gamma}:I\to CV_N$ is $K_3$-quasigeodesic, with respect to both $d_C$ and $d_C^{sym}$,  and $\underline{\gamma}(I)\subset CV_{N,\epsilon_1}$. Since $1\ne w\in H$, it follows that $w$ is fully irreducible as an element of $Out(F_N)$. Hence $w$ can be represented by an expanding irreducible train-track map $f:G\to G$ with the Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue $\lambda(f)$ equal to the stretch factor $\lambda(w)$ of the outer automorphism $w\in Out(F_N)$. There exists a volume-one ``eigenmetric" $d_f$ on $G$ with respect to which $f$ is a local $\lambda(f)$-homothety.  Then, if we view $(G,d_f)$ as a point of $CV_N$, then $d_C(G,Gw)=\log\lambda(w)$.  Moreover, in this case we can construct a $w$-periodic $d_C$-geodesic folding line $\rho:\mathbb R\to CV_N$ with the property that for any integer $i$, $\rho(i)=Gw^i$, hence for integers $i<j$ $d_C(Gw^i,Gw^j)=(j-i)\log\lambda(w)$. Thus, for any $i>0$ we have $d_C(G, w^{-i}G)=i\log\lambda(w)$.

The bi-infinite lines $\rho$ and $\underline{\gamma}$ are both $w^{-1}$-periodic (in the sense of the left action of $w^{-1}$) and therefore $\sup_{t\in \mathbb R} d_C^{sym}(\underline\gamma(t),\rho(t))<\infty$.

Hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:DT}, there exist constants $D>0$ and $\epsilon>0$ (independent of $w$) such that $\rho\subset CV_{N,\epsilon}$ and that $d_{Haus}(\rho,\underline\gamma))\le D$.  The fact that $\rho\subset CV_{N,\epsilon}$ implies that $\rho$ is a $K_4$-quasigeodesic with respect to $d_C^{sym}$ for some constant $K_4\ge 1$ independent of $w$. Now for the asymptotic translation length $||w||_{CV}$, where $w$ is viewed as an isometry of $(CV_N, d_C^{sym})$, we get that one one hand (using the line $\rho$)
\[
\frac{1}{K_4}\log\lambda(w^{-1})\le ||w||_{CV} \le K_4 \log \lambda(w^{-1})
\]
and on the other hand (using the line $\underline\gamma$) that

\[
\frac{1}{K_3}n\le ||w||_{CV} \le K_3 n.
\]

Therefore

\[
\frac{1}{K_3K_4}n\le \log\lambda(w^{-1}) \le K_3K_4n.
\]
Recall also, that by a result of Handel and Mosher~\cite{HM}, there exists a constant $M=M(N)\ge 1$ such that for every fully irreducible $\varphi\in Out(F_N)$ we have $\frac{1}{M}\le \frac{\log\lambda(\varphi)}{\log\lambda(\varphi^{-1})}\le M$.
Therefore for $w$ as above we have 


\[
\frac{1}{K_3K_4M}n\le \log\lambda(w) \le K_3K_4Mn.
\]

Recall that $\mathcal A=\{a,b\}$ and that $S$ is a finite generating set for $Out(F_N)$. Put $M'=\max\{|a|_S,|b|_S\}$, so that for every freely reduced word $w$ in $H$ we have $|w|_S\le M'|w|_\mathcal A$. 

For $R>> 1$ put $n=\lfloor \frac{R}{M'}\rfloor$.  The number of distinct $H$-conjugacy classes represented by cyclically reduced words $w$ of length $n$ is $\ge 2^n$ for $n$ big enough. 
Recall two elements of $H$ are conjugate in $H$ of and only if they are conjugate in $Out(F_N)$.  Therefore we get

\[
\ge 2^n\ge 2^{ \frac{R}{M'}-1}
\] distinct $Out(F_N)$-conjugacy classes from such words $w$.  As we have seen above, each such $w$ gives us a fully irreducible element of $Out(F_N)$ with 

\[
\frac{1}{K_3K_4M}\frac{R}{2M'}\le \log\lambda(w) \le K_3K_4Mn\le K_3K_4M \frac{R}{M'},
\] 
and the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:A} is verified.
nodes.statement_short: Take the free subgroup H from Theorem 1.3 for the free factor complex; compare translation lengths via Dowdall-Taylor fellow travelling. Word length n then gives log stretch factor ~n and 2^n conjugacy classes.

nodes.name: Take H from Theorem 1.3 applied to the free factor complex
nodes.statement: By \cite{BF}, the action of $Out(F_N)$ on $\mathcal F_N$ satisfies the hypothesis of Theorem~\ref{thm:C}. Let $H$ be the subgroup provided by Theorem \ref{thm:C} with $L=Out(F_n)$.
nodes.statement_short: Take H from Theorem 1.3 applied to the free factor complex

nodes.name: Fix a free basis of H
nodes.statement: We fix a free basis $\mathcal A=\{a,b\}$ for the free group $H$, and let $d_\mathcal A$ be the corresponding word metric on $H$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a free basis of H

nodes.name: Elements of H are fully irreducible; geodesics map to quasigeodesics
nodes.statement: Note that the assumptions on $H$ imply that every nontrivial element of $H$ is fully irreducible.  Moreover, if we pick a base-point $p$ in $\mathcal F_N$, then there is $K\ge 1$ such that the image of every geodesic in the Cayley graph $Cay(H,\mathcal A)$ in $\mathcal F_N$ under the orbit map is a (parameterized) $K$-quasigeodesic.
nodes.statement_short: Elements of H are fully irreducible; geodesics map to quasigeodesics

nodes.name: Orbit map to Outer space is a QI embedding into a thick part
nodes.statement:
Pick a basepoint $G_0\in CV_N$.
Since the projection $\pi:(CV_N,d_C)\to \mathcal F_N$ is coarsely Lipschitz~\cite{BF}, and since the orbit map $H\to \mathcal F_N$ is a quasi-isometric embedding, it follows that the orbit map $(H,d_\mathcal A)\to (CV_N,d_C), u\mapsto u G_0$ is a $K_1$-quasi-isometric embedding for some $K_1\ge 1$. Moreover, the image of this orbit map lives in an $\epsilon_0$-thick part of $CV_N$ (where $\epsilon_0$ is the injectivity radius of $G_0$). Since on $CV_{N,\epsilon_0}$ the metrics $d_C$ and $d_C^{sym}$ are bi-Lipschitz equivalent, it follows that the orbit map $(H,d_\mathcal A)\to (CV_N,d_C^{sym}), u\mapsto u G_0$ is a $K_2$-quasi-isometric embedding for some $K_2\ge 1$.
nodes.statement_short: Orbit map to Outer space is a QI embedding into a thick part

nodes.name: Build paths in CV_N from geodesics in Cay(H)
nodes.statement:
For every $c\in \mathcal{A}^{\pm 1}$ fix a $d_C$-geodesic $\tau_c$ from $G_0$ to $cG_0$. 

Now let $\gamma: I\to Cay(H,\mathcal A)$ be a geodesic such that $\gamma^{-1}(H)=I\cap \mathbb Z$ and such that the endpoints of $I$ (if any) are integers. We then define a path $\underline{\gamma}:I\to CV_N$ as follows. Whenever $n\in \mathbb Z$ is such that $[n,n+1]\subseteq I$, then $\gamma(n)=g$ and $\gamma(n+1)=gc$ for some $c\in \mathcal A^{\pm 1}$. In this case we define $\gamma|_{[n,n+1]}$ to be $g\tau_c$.  Then for every geodesic $\gamma: I\to Cay(H,\mathcal A)$ as above the path $\underline{\gamma}:I\to CV_N$ is $K_3$-quasigeodesic, with respect to both $d_C$ and $d_C^{sym}$, for some $K_3\ge 1$ independent of $\gamma$.
nodes.statement_short: Build paths in CV_N from geodesics in Cay(H)

nodes.name: Periodic geodesic for a cyclically reduced word w
nodes.statement: Let $w$ be a cyclically reduced word of length $n\ge 1$ in $H$. Consider the bi-infinite $w^{-1}$-periodic geodesic $\gamma:\mathbb R\to Cay(H,\mathcal A)$ with $\gamma(0)=1$ and $\gamma(n)=w^{-1}$.   Thus the path the path $\underline{\gamma}:I\to CV_N$ is $K_3$-quasigeodesic, with respect to both $d_C$ and $d_C^{sym}$,  and $\underline{\gamma}(I)\subset CV_{N,\epsilon_1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Periodic geodesic for a cyclically reduced word w

nodes.name: Train track representative and periodic folding line
nodes.statement: Since $1\ne w\in H$, it follows that $w$ is fully irreducible as an element of $Out(F_N)$. Hence $w$ can be represented by an expanding irreducible train-track map $f:G\to G$ with the Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue $\lambda(f)$ equal to the stretch factor $\lambda(w)$ of the outer automorphism $w\in Out(F_N)$. There exists a volume-one ``eigenmetric" $d_f$ on $G$ with respect to which $f$ is a local $\lambda(f)$-homothety.  Then, if we view $(G,d_f)$ as a point of $CV_N$, then $d_C(G,Gw)=\log\lambda(w)$. Thus, for any $i>0$ we have $d_C(G, w^{-i}G)=i\log\lambda(w)$.
nodes.statement_short: Train track representative and periodic folding line

nodes.name: The two lines have the same endpoints
nodes.statement: The bi-infinite lines $\rho$ and $\underline{\gamma}$ are both $w^{-1}$-periodic (in the sense of the left action of $w^{-1}$) and therefore $\sup_{t\in \mathbb R} d_C^{sym}(\underline\gamma(t),\rho(t))<\infty$.
nodes.statement_short: The two lines have the same endpoints

nodes.name: Apply Dowdall-Taylor to compare log stretch factor with n
nodes.statement:
Hence, by Proposition~\ref{prop:DT}, there exist constants $D>0$ and $\epsilon>0$ (independent of $w$) such that $\rho\subset CV_{N,\epsilon}$ and that $d_{Haus}(\rho,\underline\gamma))\le D$.  The fact that $\rho\subset CV_{N,\epsilon}$ implies that $\rho$ is a $K_4$-quasigeodesic with respect to $d_C^{sym}$ for some constant $K_4\ge 1$ independent of $w$. Now for the asymptotic translation length $||w||_{CV}$, where $w$ is viewed as an isometry of $(CV_N, d_C^{sym})$, we get that one one hand (using the line $\rho$)
\[
\frac{1}{K_4}\log\lambda(w^{-1})\le ||w||_{CV} \le K_4 \log \lambda(w^{-1})
\]
and on the other hand (using the line $\underline\gamma$) that

\[
\frac{1}{K_3}n\le ||w||_{CV} \le K_3 n.
\]

Therefore

\[
\frac{1}{K_3K_4}n\le \log\lambda(w^{-1}) \le K_3K_4n.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Apply Dowdall-Taylor to compare log stretch factor with n

nodes.name: Handel-Mosher passes from w^{-1} to w
nodes.statement:
Recall also, that by a result of Handel and Mosher~\cite{HM}, there exists a constant $M=M(N)\ge 1$ such that for every fully irreducible $\varphi\in Out(F_N)$ we have $\frac{1}{M}\le \frac{\log\lambda(\varphi)}{\log\lambda(\varphi^{-1})}\le M$.
Therefore for $w$ as above we have 


\[
\frac{1}{K_3K_4M}n\le \log\lambda(w) \le K_3K_4Mn.
\]
nodes.statement_short: Handel-Mosher passes from w^{-1} to w

nodes.name: Compare word lengths: M'
nodes.statement: Recall that $\mathcal A=\{a,b\}$ and that $S$ is a finite generating set for $Out(F_N)$. Put $M'=\max\{|a|_S,|b|_S\}$, so that for every freely reduced word $w$ in $H$ we have $|w|_S\le M'|w|_\mathcal A$.
nodes.statement_short: Compare word lengths: M'

nodes.name: Count at least 2^n conjugacy classes
nodes.statement:
For $R>> 1$ put $n=\lfloor \frac{R}{M'}\rfloor$.  The number of distinct $H$-conjugacy classes represented by cyclically reduced words $w$ of length $n$ is $\ge 2^n$ for $n$ big enough. 
Recall two elements of $H$ are conjugate in $H$ of and only if they are conjugate in $Out(F_N)$.  Therefore we get

\[
\ge 2^n\ge 2^{ \frac{R}{M'}-1}
\] distinct $Out(F_N)$-conjugacy classes from such words $w$.
nodes.statement_short: Count at least 2^n conjugacy classes

nodes.name: Stretch factor bounds; conclude Theorem 1.1
nodes.statement:
As we have seen above, each such $w$ gives us a fully irreducible element of $Out(F_N)$ with 

\[
\frac{1}{K_3K_4M}\frac{R}{2M'}\le \log\lambda(w) \le K_3K_4Mn\le K_3K_4M \frac{R}{M'},
\] 
and the statement of Theorem~\ref{thm:A} is verified.
nodes.statement_short: Stretch factor bounds; conclude Theorem 1.1

nodes.name: Remark 3.2 (expected double exponential growth)
nodes.statement:
As noted in the introduction, unlike in the mapping class group case, we expect that for $N\ge 3$ the number of $Out(F_N)$-conjugacy classes of fully irreducibles $\varphi\in Out(F_N)$ with $\log\lambda(\varphi)\le R$ grows as a double exponential in $R$. A double exponential upper bound follows from general Perron-Frobenius considerations. Every fully irreducible $\varphi\in Out(F_N)$ can be represented by an expanding irreducible train track map $f:G\to G$, where $G$ is a finite connected graph with $b_1(G)=N$ and with all vertices in $G$ of degree $\le 3$. The number of possibilities for such $G$ is finite in terms of $N$. By \cite[Proposition~A.4]{KB}, if $f$ is as above and $\lambda:=\lambda(f)$, then 
$\max m_{ij}\le k \lambda^{k+1}$ (where $k$ is the number of edges in $G$ and $M=(m_{ij})_{ij}$ is the transition matrix of $f$). If $\log \lambda\le R$, we get $\max \log m_{ij} \le \log k + (k+1) R$ and $\max m_{ij}\le k e^{(k+1)R}$. Thus we get exponentially many (in terms of $R$) possibilities for the transition matrix $M$ of $f$. Since for a given length $L$ there are exponentially many paths of length $L$ in $G$, this yields an (a priori) double exponential upper bound for the number of train track maps representing fully irreducible elements of $Out(F_N)$ with $\log\lambda \le R$.

For the prospective double exponential lower bound we give the following explicit construction for the case of $F_3$.  Let $w\in F(b,c)$ be a nontrivial positive word containing the subwords $b^2$, $c^2$, $bc$ and $cb$.  Consider the automorphism $\varphi_w$ of $F_3=F(a,b,c)$ defined as $\varphi_w(a)=b$, $\varphi_w(b)=c$, $\varphi_w(c)=aw(b,c)$. We can also view $\varphi_w$ as a graph map $f_w:R_3\to R_3$ where $R_3$ is the $3$-rose with the petals marked by $a$, $b$, $c$.  Then $f_w$ is an expanding irreducible train track map representing $\varphi_w$. Moreover, a direct check shows that, under the assumptions made on $w$, the Whitehead graph of $f_w$ is connected. Additionally, for a given $n\ge 1$, ``most" positive words of length $n$ in $F(b,c)$ satisfy the above conditions and define fully irreducible automorphisms $\varphi_w$. To see this, observe that the free-by-cyclic group $G_{w}=F_3\rtimes_{\varphi_w} \mathbb Z$ can be rewritten as a one-relator group:
\begin{gather*}
G_w=\langle a,b,c,t| t^{-1}at=b, t^{-1}bt=c, t^{-1}ct=aw(b,c)\rangle=\\
\langle a, t | t^{-3}at^3=aw(t^{-1}at, t^{-2}at^2)\rangle.
\end{gather*}
Moreover, one can check that if $w$ was a $C'(1/20)$ word, then the above one-relator presentation of $G_w$ satisfies the $C'(1/6)$ small cancellation condition, and therefore $G_w$ is word-hyperbolic and the automorphism $\varphi_w\in Out(F_3)$ is atoroidal. Since, as noted above, $\varphi_w$ admits an expanding irreducible train track map on the rose with connected Whitehead graph, a result of Kapovich~\cite{Ka} implies that $\varphi$ is fully irreducible. Moreover, if $|w|=L$, then it is not hard to check that  $\log \lambda(f_w)=\log\lambda(\varphi_w)$ grows like $\log L$.

Since ``random" positive words $w\in F(b,c)$ are $C'(1/20)$ and contain $b^2,c^2,cb,bc$ as subwords, for sufficiently large $R\ge 1$, the above construction produces doubly exponentially many atoroidal fully irreducible automorphisms $\varphi_w$ with $|w|=e^R$ and $\log\lambda(\varphi_w)$ on the order of $R$.  We conjecture that in fact most of these elements are pairwise non-conjugate in $Out(F_3)$ and that this method yields doubly exponentially many fully irreducible elements $\varphi$ of $Out(F_3)$ with $\log\lambda(\varphi)\le R$. However, verifying this conjecture appears to require some new techniques and ideas beyond the reach of this paper.
nodes.statement_short: Heuristics that the number of Out(F_N)-conjugacy classes of fully irreducibles with log stretch factor at most R grows doubly exponentially: Perron-Frobenius upper bound and an F_3 construction.
